chunks.subject: AP Comparative Government
chunks.title: Q2 Quantitative Analysis (5 points) — Set 1: Corruption Perceptions Index & legitimacy
chunks.content: AP Comparative Government FRQ 2 is Quantitative Analysis, 5 points, one per part (A–E), based on a data graph. Task pattern: A identify a value from the data, B describe a trend in the data, C describe a course concept, D draw a data-based conclusion, E explain what the data imply about a relationship. Set 1 answer key (Corruption Perceptions Index graph): A [1] country with highest perceived corruption in 2015 = Nigeria. B [1] describe China's CPI-score trend 2018–2021 (score increased / perceived corruption decreased). C [1] describe political legitimacy (people's belief that the government has the right to rule; sources include elections, transparency, tradition, performance). D [1] draw a conclusion explaining the UK's low perceived corruption (free/fair elections, transparency, consolidated democracy, rule of law). E [1] explain what the data imply about corruption vs. legitimacy in China (e.g., little correlation — high legitimacy from economic performance despite moderate corruption; or govt reduced corruption to maintain legitimacy). Common failure: for C, defining legitimacy as the ability to hold/maintain power rather than the people's belief in the right to rule; for D, restating score changes instead of giving a reason.

chunks.subject: AP Comparative Government
chunks.title: Q2 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2A, 5/5
chunks.content: Q2 (Set 1) scored 5/5. A: Nigeria. B: slight increase in China's CPI score → perceived corruption decreased. C: legitimacy as the government's right to rule based on citizen perception. D: UK's fair/competitive elections with minimal corruption explain its high score. E: corruption and legitimacy in China are not necessarily correlated — high legitimacy comes from economic prosperity despite a low CPI score. Full-credit model.

chunks.subject: AP Comparative Government
chunks.title: Q2 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2B, 3/5
chunks.content: Q2 (Set 1) scored 3/5. Earned A (Nigeria), B (score went up), and D (UK consolidated democracy → transparency/audits). Lost C (defined legitimacy as the ability to maintain power, not the people's belief in the right to rule) and E (cited the military as a legitimacy source but never linked it to the perception of corruption). Shows the frequent legitimacy-definition error.

chunks.subject: AP Comparative Government
chunks.title: Q2 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2C, 2/5
chunks.content: Q2 (Set 1) scored 2/5. Earned A (Nigeria) and B (score increased). Lost C (defined legitimacy via government actions rather than citizen belief in the right to rule), D (described the UK's score changes rather than a reason for low corruption), and E (connected corruption and legitimacy but named no government action linking higher corruption to lower legitimacy). Illustrates a data-reading response that misses the conceptual and explanatory parts.
